Text.Text: Force-Bonded Beast. The thread is whole in you now, both directions, always. Nothing left in that den can teach either of you anything new. Go. Mind the thread; it minds you back.
Your beast is listening. Are you? Reach rank 50 in Beast Mastery yourself before we go further. I won't ask it to bear a lesson its keeper isn't ready to learn.

A bond ought to be chosen from both ends. Six Force-Bonded Beast adepts in the Grotto Apex Den have found ways to make that choice for their animals. Defeat the six and bring me their den slate. I want to see what they call consent.
Take my key into the Grotto Caverns and find the Apex Den entrance. Your beast needn't prove anything to those keepers. Let it trust you.

A true bond is spoken, not forced. Thread laid between two willing lives, tightened by trust instead of chain. The den's keepers found the old rite and cut the willing part out of it entirely. What is left, they teach the adepts. It is not binding. It is leashing with extra words.

In the old rite, the slate marked where the ground itself remembered a bond made honestly, a place returned to, generation after generation. The adepts use it now to find beasts still uncorrupted, so they can corrupt them first. Bring it back and the ground remembers correctly again.

Because a forced bond always turns, eventually, and they know it. Better to sever a thread themselves than let it snap back on them later. That is the whole of their doctrine: control the ending, since they cannot control the truth of the beginning.
Six adepts in the Grotto Apex Den. Bring their slate back to the Waterfall Ruins. Keep listening to your beast along the way.
The thread between you is thicker already. Show me what you carried out.
The ground remembers again. That is no small thing. Rest, both of you. There is a second knot to tie, when you are ready.
Five specialists use a resonant fang charm to hold those bonds in place. Beat the five in the den and bring the charm to me. Let the beasts decide what they do when the pull is gone.
The charm comes back to the Waterfall Ruins. Let your beast tell you what it thinks of the den before you lead it in.

The fang charm once marked a bond strong enough to hum on its own, no rite needed to prove it. The specialists wear it stolen, to borrow a hum they never earned. Take it back and the hum means something again.

Force a bond, and somewhere under the obedience the beast is still choosing, every single day, not to break your neck. That choice does not vanish. It waits. A forced bond is a debt that always comes due, usually at the worst possible moment for whoever forced it.

They starve the beast of the choice entirely, goad and reward until there is no space left to choose anything else. It looks like loyalty. It is closer to drowning slowly enough that the beast forgets water used to feel different.
The five specialists in the den have the resonant fang charm. Bring it here after you've broken their hold.
The hum is on you both now. Let me hear it properly.
True again. Second knot, tied honest. You are further along this rite than either of you know yet.

The warden carries the den's apex totem. Every frightened creature there has learned to answer it. Challenge him in the Grotto Apex Den and return the totem when he's beaten. Bring companions who know when to give a beast room.
Go to the gate together, all your threads at once. He will feel more than one coming. Let him. That is the point.
Forced so long the beast inside it has forgotten it was ever asked. I do not know if there is anything left in there to save. That is not pity talking. It is the truest answer I have.

The cracked apex totem once marked the den's oldest honest bond, the first thread the rite was ever spoken over. He wears it broken because he broke that thread himself, the day forcing became easier than asking. Bring it back whole and the first bond is honored again, even after everything.

Other hunters can notice the strain you miss while you're fighting. Your beast can notice it too. Keep listening to each other. The warden is used to making his animals obey through everything they feel.
Call the warden at the Grotto Apex Den's challenge marker. Beat him and bring me the apex totem.
All your threads, still whole, still tied. Let me see what came off him.
The first bond, honored again. That is a rite older than this den's corruption, spoken true for the first time in longer than I want to guess. The inner cord will have felt that.

Four keepers still hold the den-mother's fang token. With it, they can claim authority over every bond in that den. Defeat the four and bring it here. We will leave that authority unclaimed for a while.
Bring the fang token here. We won't claim a bond just because a relic says we can.

Every corruption I have named to you, they wrote down and taught as if it were the original rite. Force. Leash. Goad. Sever what turns on you first. Scripture is a powerful lie when the ones reading it never knew the true words to compare it against.

The den-mother's own bond, older than any of us, split four ways so no single keeper could ever claim the whole truth of her thread. Whole again, it is proof the true rite still exists somewhere underneath everything they built on top of it.

The rite, spoken honestly, over every beast still capable of choosing. Not leashed. Not goaded. Asked, the way it was always meant to be asked. I have waited a long time to speak it properly again. You are the reason I finally will.
Four keepers in the den still have the fang token. Defeat them and return it to me.
Every bond among you still whole. Show me the token.

Whole, and warm with the truth again. One thread left down there, and it is the one every other thread was copied from, badly. You are close enough now that I will speak plainly: you are ready for the last knot.

The master waits in the Sealed Apex Den. Call him at the challenge marker and defeat him. Listen to your beast before you follow his lead; he has spent years making obedience feel like choice. Come back together when it's done.
Then go, all of you, as one weave. He will feel every thread coming. Let him feel exactly how many.

A bond kept so long without consent that consent stopped mattering to it. His beast does not choose him anymore, not because it loves him too much to leave, but because the choosing itself was carved out long ago. What you have built with yours this whole trial, freely, both ways, he has the same shape of, forced. That is what you are ending.

He knows how to pull your attention where he wants it. Companions can give you time to recover, but the first thing is to listen to your own beast. Don't let the strength of his bond make you distrust yours.

The rite goes back to being spoken, not forced. I will speak it honestly again, over every bond that still wants speaking. Whether the den itself heals is not mine to promise. That the rite survives, true, is.
The Sealed Apex Den has the master's challenge marker. Defeat him and come back here with your beast.
Still. The whole den, still, and threads I have not felt settle in longer than I can say. Tell me it is done.

You came back together. That's the part I wanted to see. Take your pay and let your beast rest. When you're both ready, we can begin the work of a Force-Bonded Beast. Neither of you has to be dragged into it.
Back to the thread.
I'll end the six and bring the slate.
What is this rite of binding?
What did the slate hold, once?
Why do the adepts sever threads?
Give us time.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Grotto Track Slate.
Back to the thread.
I'll end the five and bring the charm.
What did the charm hold, in the old rite?
Why does a forced bond always turn?
What do the specialists actually do to the beasts?
The thread needs settling first.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Resonant Fang Charm.
Back to the thread.
We'll bring our own bonds and cut his weave apart.
What is his bond, now?
What did the totem mark, in the old rite?
Why does one thread fail against a weave?
Our bonds are not ready to share the work.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Cracked Apex Totem, whole.
Back to the thread.
We'll cut every strand of their cord together.
What did they braid into scripture?
What did the den-mother's token hold?
What will you restore, once the relics are whole?
Let the cord hold a little longer. We are not ready.
Here's the Force-Bonded Beast Den-Mother's Fang Token, whole.
Back to the thread.
All our bonds, together, against his.
What has his bond become?
Why does it take all of us to break one bond?
What happens after, to the rite itself?
Not yet. Our threads need to be surer.
It's done. His weave broke.
